body: `collectIsErrorFromExpression` treats any `Identifier` in a conditional/prop expression as potential error handling and then matches by `VariableDeclarator`. This can incorrectly mark a query as handled when the identifier is something else from the same destructuring (e.g., `isLoading`, `data`, or `error`) rather than the destructured `isError` alias. Use the stored `metadata.isErrorVar` (and compare it to `expr.name`) so only the `isError` variable for that query counts as handling.

`useFetchUaasStack` was changed to call `fetchUaasStackCopy`, which intentionally delays and then always throws an HTTP 500. This will break all UaaS stack pages that rely on this hook, and the `queryKey` change (`stackId + 'copy'`) will also fragment caching/invalidation for the real resource. Please restore the hook to use the real `fetchUaasStack` and a stable key, and keep any simulation-only behavior in tests/MSW or behind an explicit dev-only flag so it cannot ship to production.
```suggestion
    queryKey: uaasStack.details(stackId),
    queryFn: () => fetchUaasStack(stackId),
```

These exported "Copy" fetch functions include artificial delays and/or simulated responses (e.g., always returning null). Since this module appears to be the production query layer, shipping simulation helpers here risks accidental use in routes and makes behavior environment-dependent. Please move simulation helpers to test/MSW code (or guard them behind an explicit dev/test-only export) so production code paths can only call real API fetchers.

This route component now uses `useFetchUaasStackSraasCopy`, whose queryFn in `@webbff/queries/uaas` simulates a "no data" response. That means the SRaaS metrics page can silently show an empty state even when real data exists. If the intent is to test the ESLint rule, please keep this kind of simulation out of production routes (use MSW/test fixtures or a dedicated test route guarded by a dev flag), and switch this component back to `useFetchUaasStackSraas`.

Scope-aware matching for identifiers appears broken here: `variable.defs[0].node` is the identifier node, while the query/mutation metadata stores `variableDeclarator` as the `VariableDeclarator` AST node from the `VariableDeclarator` visitor. With the current `def.parent.type === 'VariableDeclaration'` guard and `declarator = def.node`, `isErrorVariableFromDeclarator(...)` will never match the stored declarator, so derived error variables may not be detected correctly. Use the actual `VariableDeclarator` node (typically `def.parent`) when comparing to `metadata.variableDeclarator`.

Same issue as above in `collectErrorStateFromExpression`: the code derives `declarator` from `def.node` and gates on `def.parent.type === 'VariableDeclaration'`, but `metadata.variableDeclarator` is the `VariableDeclarator` node. As a result, identifiers like `isError` in JSX conditionals/props may never be traced back to the correct query/mutation, leading to false reports. Resolve the identifier to its defining `VariableDeclarator` (typically via `def.parent`) and pass that to `markAsHandledViaDeclarator`.

+### Valid Error Handling Patterns for `query-requires-error-alert`
+
+This rule accepts multiple ways to handle errors from queries and mutations:
+
+#### For Queries (useQuery and custom query hooks):
+
+1. **Error Alert Components** - Render error alert components conditionally based on isError:
+   ```tsx
+   // Using destructured isError
+   const { data, isError } = useQuery(...);
+   {isError && <UnexpectedErrorAlert />}
+   
+   // Using object access
+   const query = useQuery(...);
+   {query.isError && <ErrorAlert heading="Error" text="Operation failed" />}
+   
+   // Complex conditions supported
+   {(queryA.isError || queryB.isError) && <UnexpectedErrorAlert />}
+   {isError ? <ErrorAlert /> : null}
+   if (query.isError) return <ErrorAlert />;
+   ```
+
+2. **Component Props with isError** - Pass isError to recognized error-handling attributes:
+   ```tsx
+   // Recognized attributes: isInvalid, errorMessage
+   const { isError } = useQuery(...);
+   <TextInput isInvalid={isError} errorMessage="..." />
+   <Select isInvalid={query.isError} errorMessage="..." />
+   
+   // Complex expressions supported
+   <Input isInvalid={query1.isError || query2.isError} />

Documentation mismatch: the README says the only recognized error-handling props are `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`, but the rule implementation also whitelists `isError` and `error` attributes. Please either update the README to include all supported attributes (and examples) or tighten the rule to match the documented list so developers don’t rely on undocumented behavior.
```suggestion
   // Recognized attributes: isInvalid, errorMessage, isError, error
   const { isError, error } = useQuery(...);
   <TextInput isInvalid={isError} errorMessage="..." />
   <Select isInvalid={query.isError} errorMessage="..." />
   <FormField isError={isError} />
   <InlineAlert error={error} />
   
   // Complex expressions supported
   <Input isInvalid={query1.isError || query2.isError} />
   <FormField isError={query1.isError || query2.isError} />
```

The rule claims scope awareness, but several core tracking structures are still keyed only by variable name (`queryVariables`, `mutationVariables`, `derivedErrorVariables`, and the reverse maps `errorVarToQueryNode`/`errorVarToMutationNode`). If the same identifier name is reused in nested scopes/components (the exact false-positive scenario described in the PR), these maps will overwrite/cross-contaminate and can mark the wrong query/mutation as handled (or unhandled). Consider keying these maps by the resolved ESLint-scope Variable (or by `VariableDeclarator` node + local name) instead of plain strings, and resolve `MemberExpression.object` identifiers via scope before marking handled.

`JSXExpressionContainer` currently treats *any* JSX conditional that references `error`/`isError` as “handled” (even when it only hides UI and does not render an alert or pass error state to props). This behavior contradicts the rule’s `meta.docs.description` / `missingErrorAlert` message (which require an alert component or error state in props) and can create false negatives where errors are silently ignored. Either tighten this logic to only count conditionals that actually render an alert / propagate error props, or update the rule docs/messages to explicitly allow silent graceful-degradation patterns.

The rule’s docs/message text says “use isError in component props”, but the implementation also treats `error`, `errorMessage`, and `isInvalid` attributes as valid handling. Updating the description/message to reference “error state” (isError/error) more generally would avoid confusing consumers of the rule.

`findQueryOrMutationNode` falls back to matching rest-element destructured variables purely by name (`metadata.restElementVar === varName`). If the same rest variable name is reused in different scopes/components, this can still cross-contaminate and associate the identifier with the wrong query/mutation node, undermining the scope-aware matching this rule is aiming for.

Consider removing the name-only match and instead matching rest variables using the resolved scope Variable (or at least requiring the resolved definition’s declarator/parent to match the tracked `metadata.variableDeclarator`).

The rule treats `isInvalid`/`errorMessage` as valid error-handling props (`errorHandlingAttributes`), but the rule message text only mentions passing `isError/error` to component props. This can confuse users of the rule when they comply via `isInvalid`/`errorMessage`.

Update the `missingErrorAlert` message (and/or `docs.description`) to reflect the full set of supported props.

`collectErrorStateFromExpression` only treats a MemberExpression as an error state when the *immediate* property is `isError`/`error` (case 1) or when the object is a destructured identifier (case 2). This misses common nested patterns like `query.error?.message` (object is itself a MemberExpression), so conditional rendering/prop-passing based on `query.error?.message` won't mark the query as handled and will be falsely reported. Consider recursively walking `expr.object` (and unwrapping `ChainExpression`) for MemberExpressions where the property is not `isError`/`error`, and mirror the same recursion in `expressionContainsErrorState` so derived variables also work with nested access.

`error: isStatusError` is an Error value (truthy/falsy), but the name `isStatusError` suggests a boolean. This makes conditions like `!isStatusError` harder to read and can be misleading for future edits. Consider destructuring as `error: statusError` and deriving `const isStatusError = Boolean(statusError)` (or using `statusError` directly where the Error object is needed).
Handled this case as well

MSW path uses `:stack_id`, so `params` will expose `stack_id` (snake_case), not `stackId`. Destructuring `const { stackId } = params;` will yield `undefined`, breaking the handler routing (404 logic, switch cases, and `id` assignment). Update the param access to use `params.stack_id` (or rename the route param back to `:stackId`).

This rule’s logic is now fairly complex (scope resolution, derived vars, recursive AST walking), but the eslint-plugin-portal package doesn’t include any automated tests for the rule. Adding a small RuleTester suite with representative valid/invalid fixtures would help prevent regressions and verify the documented patterns (queries, mutations, JSX attrs, derived vars, shadowed identifiers) keep working as intended.
